key_insight: AeroZoo shows that boundary-condition inputs are crucial for aerodynamic surrogates, while unseen enclosures and boundary-condition layouts remain harder than unseen geometry families.
engineering_relevance: Reliable CFD surrogates must generalize across shapes, enclosures and operating conditions—not just predict variations within one design family.
method: Assemble 3,815 time-mean RANS solutions with transition modeling across seven geometry families, eight enclosure configurations and Reynolds numbers from 10³ to 10⁸.
Specify each PDE problem using boundary meshes grouped by condition type, prescribed values and fluid properties.
Evaluate two tasks using engineering metrics and 22 frozen, geometry-disjoint splits.
evidence_signal: On the random split, boundary-condition tokens reduced GeoTransolver’s median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of inlet speed in single-seed runs; ISLA achieved 5.3% over four seeds.
watch_item: The canonical benchmark includes only 2,816 samples with stable time means, and held-out enclosures or boundary-condition layouts increased ISLA’s error by 2.4–9.2×.
paper_title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
